target: Domain.fs bucket(); configurations.csv CFG-4/CFG-5/CFG-7
finding: Routing by responsible_entity overrides configuration. Any activity whose responsible_entity or human_role is 'sponsor' goes to SponsorOwned before the INDEPENDENT-AUTHORIZATION, AdminJudgment or AdminException match. Its vendor share is therefore 0 in every configuration, including CFG-5, which is defined as 'vendor performs all delegable administration incl. independent authorization'. Payment batch release (OA-GRT-011), wire release (OA-GRT-014), bank-detail change verification (OA-CHR-008), manual journal and correction second approval (OA-ACG-002/008), monthly close and controller sign-off (OA-ACG-007), audit support (OA-ACG-011) and Form 990 package (OA-ACG-010) never reach vendor pools. As a result CFG-4 and CFG-5 are identical, and CFG-3/4/5 have identical AUTH load.
evidence: activity-loads-reference.csv: all of these rows have bucket=SponsorOwned and vendor_share=0. Activities classified other than SPONSOR-OWNED but bucketed SponsorOwned total about 2,087 h at $500M (controller 400 h; accounting 109 h; ops 126 h; compliance 93 h; authorizer 80 h; sponsor-role 1,192 h, mostly OA-GRT-005). headline-staffing.csv: the CFG-4 and CFG-5 rows at $500M are byte-identical.
proposed_correction: Separate legal responsibility (responsible_entity) from who performs the work. Bucket by classification first. Apply sponsor routing only to classification SPONSOR-OWNED or to activities reserved by law (CO-001/CO-003). Re-tag role 'sponsor' rows that are delegable (GRT-011, GRT-014, GRT-018, CHR-008) with a vendor role (authorizer/ops). Re-run CFG-4/5/7.
estimated_impact: CFG-5/7 vendor hours rise by about 600-800 h at $500M, excluding OA-GRT-005 (about 1,050 h more if Tier-2 review is delegated in CFG-4/5). AUTH grows from 98 h to about 480 h, roughly +$95-120k/yr fractional; FINANCE grows by about 110 h. CFG-5 View 1 cost is understated by roughly 10-15% at $500M.

target: Workload.fs hoursByRole / Staffing.fs arrivals (authorizer pool)
finding: Every independent-review minute is assigned to role 'authorizer', which sits in the AUTH pool (controller cost basis, $225/h fractional). In the reference case the whole AUTH workload is misrouted review: second approvers of control-relevant code changes (OA-TEC-010, 60 h), policy-pack approval (OA-CMP-007, 19 h), deficiency case approval (OA-CMP-012, 12 h) and kill-switch dual control (OA-CMP-021, 2 h). Code review must be done by engineers, and financial authorizers cannot do it. Meanwhile no payment-release work reaches AUTH (see ADV-OA-001).
evidence: activity-loads-reference.csv auth_minutes with vendor_share>0: TEC-010 3,600 min, CMP-007 1,152, CMP-012 720, CMP-021 144. These match simulation-reference AUTH arrived_hours of 97.6 (93.6 + 4 controller).
proposed_correction: Assign second-person minutes to an independent role within the same competence: ENG for TEC-*, COMPLIANCE for CMP-*, AUTH only for payment, journal and NAV approvals. Model that the second person must differ from the first but come from the same pool, and raise that pool's minNamed where needed.
estimated_impact: ENG +62 h/yr at $500M (absorbed by existing dedicated staff). AUTH cost of $24k is currently paying for the wrong work. Corrected AUTH depends on ADV-OA-001.

target: Staffing.fs staffPool mode rule (dedicate_threshold_fte=0.6 for all roles)
finding: The fractional-versus-dedicated switch uses a fixed 0.6 average-FTE threshold, not cost. COMPLIANCE at $500M has 794 h (0.52 FTE) bought fractionally at $190 x 1.1 = $165.9k, while a dedicated compliance owner costs $121.8k. The rule errs in both directions: the cost break-even is 583 h (0.38 FTE) for compliance and 741 h (0.48 FTE) for controller. For OPS, $70 x 1.1 makes fractional cheaper up to about 1.0 FTE.
evidence: simulation-reference.csv COMPLIANCE fractional, cost 165,851; roles.csv compliance dedicated_cost_base 121,842; parameters ZBP-018=1.1; productive hours 6.5 x (261-25) = 1,534.
proposed_correction: Choose the mode by minimum total cost (fractional incl. availability and retainer floor; dedicated incl. recruiting and backup). Apply a control or availability constraint, not a fixed threshold. Report each switch point.
estimated_impact: COMPLIANCE about -$40k/yr at $250M-$1B (the 5,000-account dedicated threshold moves to about 3,000). OPS dedication could be deferred where peaks are covered.

target: Staffing.fs minNamed: COMPLIANCE=1
finding: COMPLIANCE needs only 1 named person, yet it holds time-critical, non-delegable dispositions: sanctions alerts (OA-CMP-001, SLA 48 h), OFAC blocked or rejected reporting within 10 business days (CO-019, OA-CMP-002), fraud and account-takeover triage (OA-CMP-017, SLA 4 h) and restricted fraud investigation (OA-CMP-018, SLA 24 h). With a fractional single owner these hold all releases whenever that person is absent or busy with another client. The same person also runs control testing (OA-CMP-011) of the controls they operate, which is self-review, and CO-022 requires independent testing of the sanctions programme.
evidence: Staffing.fs minNamed returns 1.0 for COMPLIANCE. simulation-reference COMPLIANCE named_persons=1, utilisation 93%. control-obligations CO-018, CO-019, CO-022.
proposed_correction: Set minNamed COMPLIANCE=2 (backup with sanctions and fraud disposition authority). Add an external independent sanctions/AML programme test (about $10-25k/yr), or move OA-CMP-011 testing to someone other than the operator.
estimated_impact: +$8-15k/yr backup retainer (40-80 h x $190). +$10-25k/yr independent testing. At 93% utilisation, a single fractional owner leaves almost no headroom.

target: Staffing.fs (no management activity); FC-205 only in standalone view
finding: No management time is modelled outside standalone View 3. Reference staffing needs about 11 named persons across 6 pools (OPS 2, FINANCE 2, AUTH 2, COMPLIANCE 1, ENG 3, COMM 1), several of them fractional or contract. The founder is allocated 400 h, all consumed by COMM and ENG queue work. Hiring, supervision, performance management, vendor management of fractional firms, the December surge plan and training are absent. At scale the step tables reach OPS 231, FINANCE 108 and COMPLIANCE 43 FTE at 1M accounts, with no supervisors or managers.
evidence: results.md table 4 (founder 314 h ENG + 86 h COMM = 400); activity-inventory-notes s4 ('Echelon corporate functions (finance, legal, hiring) are excluded'); staffing-thresholds.csv; fixed-costs FC-205 view=standalone.
proposed_correction: Add a management activity: about 2-3 h/week per direct report, or a span of 1:7-1:10 with a team-lead step function per pool, plus about 60-120 h/yr for fractional vendor management. Charge it to the founder first and dedicated leadership afterwards. Include it in Views 1 and 2.
estimated_impact: Small scale: +400-700 founder h/yr (more than the whole 400 h allotment), or about $80-140k imputed. At scale: +10-14% of pool labour cost for leads and managers.

target: founder_hours_per_year=400 (ZBP-016); Staffing.fs founderAllocation and NamedPersons
finding: The founder is used as the third named engineer, needed to meet CNV-PLT-010 (author plus two non-author approvers), as an implied on-call participant, and as the whole COMM function. The evidence says one person holds every role, competes across 30 initiatives, 83 repositories and a consulting practice, and has no Unbound time allocation decision. With 2 engineers plus the founder, every control-relevant change needs both other people, so any single absence (about 75 person-days/yr) blocks control-relevant releases. A 1-in-3 on-call rota for a payments platform is not compatible with a 400 h/yr part-time founder.
evidence: echelon-shared notes s4, s6 (1,800 h hypothetical; 30 initiatives; 'Approver capacity ... cannot be met'); simulation-reference ENG founder_hours 314.32, named 3; parameters ZBP-043.
proposed_correction: Do not count the founder toward ENG minimum named persons or on-call. Plan for 3 employed engineers, or 2 plus a retained external approver (about 100-150 h/yr), with a fourth approver for absence continuity. Run the founder=0 case as the base for a staffed-administration offer.
estimated_impact: +$25-40k/yr (retained external approver plus on-call stipend) to +$212k/yr (third dedicated engineer). Founder imputed cost falls by about $63k.

target: Simulation.fs capacity() absence model; ZBP-013 absence_days
finding: Absence is spread evenly as a 9.6% daily capacity haircut, so a one-person pool never has zero capacity. In practice a sole dedicated OPS person takes contiguous leave (1-2 weeks, often in late December) and the pool's capacity drops to the backup. The surge or backup person in OPS is bought for only 63 h/yr (or 40 h retainer in other pools), while covering 25 absence days takes about 160 h per dedicated person. Initiation, which cannot be done by FINANCE or AUTH people because of segregation of duties, is unstaffed during those blocks.
evidence: Simulation.fs: capacity = staff x perDay x (1 - absent). simulation-reference OPS dedicated 1 + 63 surge h; ZBP-020 backup_retainer_hours 40.
proposed_correction: Simulate absence as contiguous blocks per named person (including a December blackout policy). Size the backup's paid hours as max(retainer, absence-cover hours) for every pool with fewer than 2 dedicated staff.
estimated_impact: +100-150 backup h per single-person pool, about +$10-25k/yr per pool at fractional rates (OPS, FINANCE, AUTH, COMPLIANCE).

target: roles.csv fractional rates; ZBP-018 fractional_availability_premium=1.1
finding: Fractional pools are priced as billed hours x 1.1, with no engagement floor. Examples: FINANCE 28.4 h for $2,968/yr at $100M (CFG-1), and AUTH 97.6 h for $24k, both with a 1-business-day SLA and December peaks. Fractional controllers and compliance officers typically work on monthly retainers and serve several clients, so same-day availability for releases, sanctions hits (4-48 h SLAs) or reconciliation breaks is not dependable at hourly pricing. The $190-225/h rates are plausible for the professional, but the availability that the simulation assumes is not bought by those rates.
evidence: headline-staffing.csv row 100000000,CFG-1,FINANCE: 28.4 h, cost 2967.8, simulated_fte 1.35. roles.csv basis 'ASSUMPTION'. Quotes not commissioned (ZBP-018). Owner direction ODP-02: no fractional reviewer retainer authorised.
proposed_correction: Add a minimum annual engagement per fractional named person (for example $12-36k by role) and an SLA-backed retainer premium (1.25-1.5) for pools with SLAs of 24 h or less. Obtain 2-3 quotes before relying on them. Treat outsourced accounting firms as SOC 1 subservice organisations (carve-out or inclusive).
estimated_impact: +$30-90k/yr at $100-500M (about 4-6 fractional named persons with floors). Larger relative effect on small-AUA break-even.

target: Staffing.fs surge option (OPS, FINANCE); ZBP-045/046
finding: December surge contractors are modelled as interchangeable hours (63 h/yr at $500M) plus $15k readiness. OPS includes payment initiation and identity proofing, which need background-checked, access-provisioned, trained named persons inside the initiation segregation-of-duties group. A contractor who works 63 h a year cannot keep proficiency. Temporary staff with DAF knowledge are scarce in December, when every sponsor surges at once. The surge person is also implicitly the only OPS backup (backupCost counts surge mode as covered).
evidence: Staffing.fs: the surgeAllowed branch; backupCost counts 'dedicated+surge' as a named person. simulation-reference OPS fractional_hours 62.9.
proposed_correction: Replace anonymous surge with a named, retained part-time OPS second (for example 0.2-0.3 FTE year-round, rising in Nov-Dec) who serves as backup, surge and segregation-of-duties coverage. Or design December work so that the backlog is non-initiation (support), which agency staff can do.
estimated_impact: +$15-30k/yr versus the modelled surge cost at $500M, offsetting part of the backup cost in ADV-OA-007.

target: Pool AUTH (controller + independent authorizer)
finding: Putting the controller and the payment authorizer in one pool lets the same person release payments (OA-GRT-011/014, once routed per ADV-OA-001) and sign off the reconciliation and close that would detect an improper release (OA-ACG-007, CO-041 'independent review'). CO-042 lists release and reconcile as incompatible. Two named AUTH persons do not prevent this unless one of them never releases.
evidence: roles.csv controller and authorizer share pool AUTH and independence_group AUTHORIZATION; control-obligations CO-041, CO-042.
proposed_correction: Split AUTH into RELEASE (authorizer) and CONTROLLER (sign-off) independence groups. Alternatively, add a rule that the controller of record never releases, which forces a third named person in AUTH (or uses sponsor personnel for release).
estimated_impact: +1 named retained person, about $9-20k/yr at small scale. No change once AUTH is dedicated with 2 or more staff and roles are split.

target: Pool OPS (ops + support + implementation); OA-COM-007/009/010/011
finding: Implementation is lumpy project work, but it is annualised as new_sponsor_share x sponsors (0.2 onboardings/yr at 1 sponsor) and spread as flat arrivals. One onboarding takes about 1,000-1,300 h (OA-COM-007 500 h, OA-COM-009 367 h, OA-COM-010 50 h, OA-COM-011 69 h, plus OA-COM-004). That work lands in a 3-6 month window, often aimed at go-live before year end, when the December peak hits the same pool. The first sponsor's onboarding is certain and is a precondition for revenue, but the steady state models it as 20%.
evidence: activity-loads-reference OA-COM-007 events 0.2, vendor minutes 5,100; ZBP-023 new_sponsor_share 0.2; operational-activities seasonality 'flat' for COM-007/009.
proposed_correction: Model onboarding as a discrete project with a start date and team, staffed by implementation contractors or ENG, and keep it out of the OPS queue. Add a year-1 scenario with 1 certain onboarding and forbid go-live in Nov-Dec.
estimated_impact: Year-1 (or any onboarding year): about +900-1,100 implementation h (about $110-130k at $120/h contract). Steady state is unchanged if onboarding stays at 0.2/yr.

target: Recruitment, turnover and ramp (not modelled in Views 1-2; FC-206 standalone only)
finding: Dedicated hires (ENG 2, OPS 1 at $500M, and many more at scale) carry no recruiting fee, onboarding or ramp time, and no turnover. Small single-incumbent pools turn knowledge loss into a control failure: a departing sole OPS person or engineer removes a named person needed for segregation of duties or CNV-PLT-010. Training for vendor staff (DAF rules, OFAC, Nacha) appears only implicitly in absence_days, and OA-COM-012 trains sponsor staff only.
evidence: fixed-costs.csv FC-206 'recruiting' view=standalone; no turnover parameter in parameters.csv; activity OA-COM-012 role implementation, sponsor-staff training.
proposed_correction: Add parameters for annual turnover (10-20%), recruiting cost (15-25% of salary) and ramp (2-3 months at 50% productivity). Add vendor-staff compliance training hours per named person (about 16-24 h/yr). Apply them in Views 1 and 2.
estimated_impact: About +$25-50k/yr at the 3-dedicated-FTE scale; about 5-8% of dedicated labour at scale.

target: CFG-1..4 reliance on sponsor personnel for independent authorization
finding: Sponsor staff are a sound source of independence (a different entity), but the model treats their availability as given. Small sponsors may lack two independent authority holders (CNV-GOV-003 requires three distinct persons in the release chain). Their release turnaround is outside the vendor's SLA control. Their duties become CUECs in the vendor SOC 1 (CO-045). Sponsor-borne time is valued at $70/h (ZBP-022), which undervalues controller-grade sign-off work (OA-ACG-007/011, OA-GRT-011) at about $100-125/h.
evidence: configurations.csv CFG-4 'sponsor personnel provide independent authorization'; activity-inventory-notes s4 (per-sponsor floor of about 2.5 FTE); ZBP-022 sponsor_labour_rate 50-95.
proposed_correction: Add a sponsor-readiness gate: a minimum sponsor roster check plus a fallback vendor authorizer for CFG-1..4. Value sponsor time by role (controller and authorizer at controller rate). Model release-latency risk in the December simulation.
estimated_impact: Sponsor-borne cost understated by about $15-40k/yr per sponsor. Possible fallback authorizer retainer of $10-20k/yr.

target: Workload.fs AI-ASSISTED vs OA-TEC-021 (AI agent configuration, evaluation and change control)
finding: At the reference scale AI assistance costs more than it saves. Vendor AI-ASSISTED handling is 696 h/yr, so a 0.85 factor saves about 123 h, mostly support time at about $50-75/h (about $7-9k). OA-TEC-021 adds a fixed 384 h/yr of engineering time (about $45k) plus token spend (ZBI-032..035), and ENG is the pool that forces a 2-person hire. The 0.85 factor itself is consistent with field evidence (3-14%), but the net economics do not justify AI before roughly 5-10x the reference volume.
evidence: activity-loads-reference: AI-ASSISTED vendor h (ACN-008 192.7, GRT-022 86.3, COM-007 85, TEC-007 81.6, CMP-008 68 ...), sum 696. TEC-021 vendor minutes 23,040 (384 h). parameters ZBP-001 base 0.85.
proposed_correction: Make OA-TEC-021 scale with the number of AI-assisted workflows deployed and enable AI per activity only where saved hours exceed evaluation and change-control hours. Keep deterministic plus human handling at launch. Report net AI benefit explicitly.
estimated_impact: About -$30-45k/yr at $250M-$1B if AI is deferred (ENG -300 to -384 h, which may avoid part of the founder or ENG load).

target: Silent and correlated automation failure (not priced); ZBP-027..031 incidents
finding: The model prices only detected exceptions (exception rate x minutes) and small independent incidents (for example 4 ops failures/yr x 8 h). For 97% straight-through processing, the dominant automation risk is a correlated silent error that replicates across all events until someone notices. Examples are a wrong eligibility or fee rule version, a stale charity-status feed (OA-CHR-010), a bad acknowledgment template (OA-CON-009) or a posting-rule error (OA-ACG-012). No remediation workload exists for mass re-issue, re-accrual, recovery of grants to ineligible payees, donor communications or sponsor restatement. AUTO-EXCEPTION classification also assumes that the automation detects its own exceptions.
evidence: Simulation.fs incidents(): independent Bernoulli draws with fixed hours. parameters ZBP-030/031 (4/yr x 8 h). Events 302,825 at 97.1% auto (results.md s4). No activity for mass remediation.
proposed_correction: Add a correlated-failure scenario (for example 0.3-1 per year affecting 1-10% of a quarter's events) with cross-pool remediation hours, external costs and E&O deductible. Price business-level invariant monitors and rule-change regression (shadow replay) as named activities.
estimated_impact: Expected about +$20-60k/yr. Tail event about $100-400k (remediation plus credits) per occurrence at $500M-$1B.

target: Monitoring of automation: OA-CMP-003 sampling, OA-ACG-005, FC-009, OA-TEC-001
finding: Automation monitoring is thin and partly misassigned. Independent sampling of straight-through grants (OA-CMP-003) is 0.5% of grants, about 90 samples/yr at $500M. That gives roughly a 60% chance of detecting a 1% error rate, and it is not tied to rule changes. The independent attestation sample of auto-passed reconciliations (OA-ACG-005) is routed to the sponsor even in CFG-5 (ADV-OA-001). Observability is deferred by owner decision, and FC-009 is $6k of paging SaaS. No activity covers exception-rate drift or straight-through-rate monitoring, AI output QA beyond TEC-021, or data-feed completeness (row counts and gaps).
evidence: operational-activities OA-CMP-003 freq 0.005 per grant, 15 min; OA-ACG-005 responsible sponsor; fixed-costs FC-009 base 6,000; echelon-shared notes RP-REG-2026-0001.
proposed_correction: Define statistically sized attribute sampling (for example 60 items per material rule version plus a monthly risk-weighted sample). Add an 'automation outcome monitoring' activity (drift dashboards, feed completeness, daily invariant review) at about 2-4 h/week in ENG or FINANCE, plus observability build cost in development.
estimated_impact: +100-200 h/yr (about $12-30k) plus one-time observability build of $20-60k.

target: Duplicate incident workload: OA-TEC-004 vs ZBP-024..026; OA-TEC-002 vs ZBP-030; OA-TEC-013/OA-INV-015 vs ZBP-027..029
finding: Incident response appears to be counted twice. Security incident response is an activity (OA-TEC-004, 4/yr x 1,500 min = 100 h) and is also seeded as simulation incidents (ZBP-024/025, 1/yr x 24 h ENG + 8 h OPS). Operational incident response (OA-TEC-002, 50 h per sponsor) overlaps with ops failures (ZBP-030/031). Ingestion file exceptions and custodian outages (OA-TEC-013, OA-INV-015) overlap with integration failures (ZBP-027..029). Seeded incidents carry a 1-day SLA, which also raises simulated peak FTE.
evidence: simulation-reference ENG incident_hours 104.6, OPS 40, FINANCE 32; activity-loads-reference TEC-004 vendor 100 h, TEC-002 50 h.
proposed_correction: Keep incident volumes in one place: activities for average load, seeded incidents only for timing, with activity hours reduced by the same expected amount. Document the reconciliation.
estimated_impact: About -100 to -180 h/yr across ENG, OPS and FINANCE (about -$10-20k). It may lower ENG simulated peak, but the 3-person floor dominates.

target: Simulation.fs arrivals SLA conversion and fluid model
finding: SLAs are converted as max(1, sla_hours/24) business days, while the code comment says 8 business hours per day. All sub-day SLAs become 'finish by the next business day': production on-call (OA-TEC-001, 1 h), kill switch (OA-CMP-021, 1 h), fraud and account-takeover triage (OA-CMP-017, 4 h), custodian outage (OA-INV-015, 4 h). Weekend capacity is zero, so no after-hours or on-call coverage is required or costed. Arrivals are a deterministic fluid split into daily fractions, with no Poisson variance and no case indivisibility, which understates peaks for small pools.
evidence: Simulation.fs line 'let sla = max 1.0 (l.Activity.SlaHours / 24.0)' with comment '(8 business hours per day)'; capacity()=0 on weekends; OA-TEC-001 seasonality year_end, 365 events.
proposed_correction: Model a separate on-call pool with 24x7 coverage cost (stipend about 10-15% of salary or per-shift pay, minimum rota of 4). Use intraday or stochastic arrivals for sub-day SLAs. Fix the comment or the divisor.
estimated_impact: On-call stipend +$20-40k/yr for 2-3 engineers. The engineer floor may rise to 4 for a sustainable rota (see ADV-OA-006).

target: analytic_peak_factor=1.25 (ZBP-021) vs simulation-calibration.csv
finding: Monte Carlo and break-even scans use an analytic peak factor of 1.25, described as 'calibrated against the queue simulation'. The calibration table shows ratios of 1.66-1.70 for ENG and 1.93-4.19 for OPS between 400 and 4,000 accounts, and up to 15.6 for FINANCE. Hire-step rounding hides part of the gap, but the analytic mode understates peak staffing for OPS and ENG in the scale range where break-even falls.
evidence: simulation-calibration.csv rows 2000/OPS 2.24, 4000/OPS 1.93, ENG about 1.66-1.70; parameters ZBP-021 base 1.25; Staffing.fs analytic branch.
proposed_correction: Use pool-specific and scale-specific peak factors interpolated from the calibration table, or run the simulation at the break-even grid points.
estimated_impact: Monte Carlo P50 break-even likely understated by about 3-8% (one extra OPS FTE or surge near 4,000-8,000 accounts).

target: Exception rates at steady state; ZBP-002 exception_mult 0.6-2.0; OD-M-14
finding: All exception rates are steady-state values borrowed from incumbent or EV baselines, and no Unbound measurement exists (no design partner; the synthetic time study has not run). A new platform's first 12-24 months typically show higher exception and touch rates while rules, matching tolerances, charity data and the answer corpus mature. The headline and break-even views apply mature rates from day one. The 9% Tier-2 trigger on OA-GRT-005 alone is a quarter of all human time and is unmeasured.
evidence: parameters ZBP-002 'No measured Unbound exception rates exist'; activity-inventory-notes s3 (GRT-005 = 24.3%); echelon-shared notes OD-M-14.
proposed_correction: Add a launch-phase multiplier that decays (for example 2.0x in year 1, 1.4x in year 2, 1.0x from year 3) and apply it in the working-capital and year-1 cash views. Commit to measuring touch rates in shadow replay before pricing.
estimated_impact: Year-1 human hours +40-100%. At $500M that means OPS and FINANCE move to dedicated staff 1-2 steps earlier (+$60-150k in year 1).

target: Design elimination candidates (OA-GRT-013, OA-GRT-016, OA-CON-004, OA-CHR-007, OA-ACG-004, OA-ACN-008, OA-GRT-022)
finding: Several large vendor exception queues are produced by design choices that could be removed rather than staffed. Paper-check grants (OA-GRT-013, 33% of grants) drive check exceptions and all of OA-GRT-016 (53 h) plus check printing and mail costs. Unidentified receipts (OA-CON-004, 102 h) remain at a 4% rate even though the register cites intent-first and virtual-account prevention (EV-E04 prevention 0.6). Destination verification (OA-CHR-007, 106 h at 40% exception) could use account-owner-match APIs and network reuse. Reconciliation breaks (OA-ACG-004, 142 h) could be cut by end-to-end reference IDs. Donor contacts (OA-ACN-008, 193 h) and charity payment inquiries (OA-GRT-022, 86 h) could be cut by self-service status and remittance advice.
evidence: activity-loads-reference vendor hours as cited; elimination_challenge text for CON-004 ('virtual account per fund (EV-E04 prevention 0.6)') and CHR-007 ('account-owner match API').
proposed_correction: Add PREVENTED variants with explicit prevention factors and their build and run cost. Default to ACH with a paid check opt-in. Issue a virtual account or reference per fund. Use bank-account ownership verification. Provide donor and charity status portals. Then re-run staffing.
estimated_impact: About -250 to -400 vendor h/yr at $500M (about -$20-40k labour) plus -$50-100k/yr external check costs at the 10,000-account reference. OPS dedicated threshold deferred by about 1 step.

target: Classification: AI-ASSISTED where deterministic suffices (OA-GRT-002, OA-CMP-019, OA-ACN-001)
finding: Some activities are classed AI-ASSISTED where a deterministic method is enough and easier to audit. Charity search and disambiguation (OA-GRT-002) is an EIN and registry lookup. Nacha fraud monitoring (OA-CMP-019) is normally velocity and threshold rules that auditors expect to be reproducible. Prospect questions (OA-ACN-001) can be answered from a published ProgramDescription and FAQ. AI here adds evaluation and change-control burden (OA-TEC-021) and conflicts with CO-062, with little time saved.
evidence: operational-activities classification AI-ASSISTED for GRT-002 (exception 0.01), CMP-019, ACN-001. control-obligations CO-062.
proposed_correction: Reclassify to DETERMINISTIC or AUTO-EXCEPTION with rule-based triage. Reserve AI for unstructured inputs (correspondence, documents) and review outputs by sampling.
estimated_impact: Small direct effect (<20 h/yr); it reduces the AI evaluation scope in OA-TEC-021 and simplifies audit evidence.

target: ELIMINATED rows (OA-CON-018, OA-GRT-024, OA-ACG-016) and OA-GRT-006 freq 0
finding: The 'eliminated' activities are scope exclusions (cards, foreign or expenditure-responsibility grants, UBIT), not design eliminations. An existing sponsor migrating under CFG-5 may already have card gifts, foreign grants or UBIT exposure, and that demand moves to the sponsor or blocks the sale. OA-GRT-006 (per-grant approval without board delegation) is set to zero on the assumption that every sponsor adopts deterministic delegation, which CO-004 marks UNCERTAIN. Without delegation, Tier-2-style human approval applies to 100% of grants, not 9%.
evidence: operational-activities ELIMINATED rows have freq 0 and evidence VERIFIED-FACT (scope); OA-GRT-006 freq_base 0.0; control-obligations CO-004 UNCERTAIN.
proposed_correction: Label these rows SCOPE-EXCLUDED and reflect them as an addressable-market or sponsor-qualification constraint. Add a 'no board delegation' sensitivity in which OA-GRT-006/005 apply to all grants (sponsor-borne in most configurations).
estimated_impact: Without delegation, sponsor or vendor human time rises by about 0.5-1 h per 100 grants. Market size falls for sponsors with foreign-grant books.
